rows.what_the_ink_shows: The full scan is a typescript with handwritten corrections. In crops/6_scan002_L707_date_folio.jpg the top-right handwriting reads “Pise, Mai 1966” and a separate numeral 1 marks the folio. In crops/6_scan002_L707_letter_opening.jpg the salutation is “Cher John,”; the opening says “un projet de théorie, ou plutôt” followed by inserted “de” before “début de théorie”, and the underlined heading is “Chapitre 1” / “La notion de cristal.” In crops/6_scan002_L707_nilpotent_thickenings.jpg, paragraph 1.0 defines C using R-préschémas T sous S; the arrows run S to T, and the typed condition is “une immersion fermée définie par un idéal localement nilpotent”. This passage contains no divided-power condition. In crops/6_scan002_L707_crystal_definition.jpg, Definition 1.1 calls a crystal of quasi-coherent modules “une section cartésienne de la catégorie fibrée précédente au dessus de C”. These are already represented in the original LaTeX.
rows.note: The supplied row refines a broad catalogue and mathematical assessment rather than identifying a mistranscribed phrase on this page. Preserve the whole transcription. This page itself supports the salutation John, date, folio 1, chapter heading, nilpotent closed-immersion condition and cartesian-section definition. The surname Tate, full letter range 6:2–32, folios 1–30, Pisa letterhead on 6:3 and later chapter ranges come from the supplied sweep-3 SA15 table; no other page was inspected. The table calls the construction the infinitesimal site and discusses later claims and divided-power refinements; those are background assertions, not text to interpolate here. The quoted later margin “faute d’introduire les puiss. div.” is not present on this page. All four crops use Pillow LANCZOS enlargement to 2800 pixels across and contrast factor 1.6.
